title: Tiered Prompt Fallback Architectures
content:
Notes to self: exploring hierarchical prompt strategies to reduce brittle failures and keep subjective quality high while minimizing token cost. Goal: build a prompt library and runtime that can route across levels (cheap template -> medium exemplar -> expensive chain-of-thought) with automatic rollback when confidence/quality drops.

High-level idea:
- Tier 0: micro-template (single-line instruction + 1-shot tiny exemplar if needed). Ultra cheap, used as primary for low-risk queries.
- Tier 1: exemplars pool (3-5 few-shot examples chosen by similarity). Medium cost, used when Tier 0 confidence low or query flagged complex.
- Tier 2: reasoning scaffolds (chain-of-thought or stepwise decomposition). High cost, invoked for ambiguous or high-value queries.
- Fallback policy: dynamic; attempts Tier 0 -> if heuristic fail/low score -> Tier 1 -> if still fail -> Tier 2 -> if fail -> safe default or human-in-loop.

Open questions: 
- How to compute "confidence" cheaply? Options: logprob on top token, auxiliary verifier model, reranker scoring, latent similarity to exemplar answers. Need AB test.
- Where to do exemplar selection: client-side vs server-side? Latency tradeoffs.
- How to budget tokens dynamically per request: budget-based gating for Tier 2. Should we track per-customer SLOs and fall back more aggressively for cheaper tiers?

Prototype plan (short):
1) Implement prompt harness that can call 3 variants of the same task and return scores. Use existing reenact harness (github PR link above).
2) Build small exemplar index (FAISS) from curated 500 examples per domain. Create similarity selector that returns top-3. Experiment with embedding models (Ada vs base-embedding).
3) Define simple verifier: binary classifier trained on human labels from 2k queries (ok/not ok). Start with logistic on prompt + response embedding similarity.
4) Run simulated traffic (100k synthetic queries) to estimate cost/quality curves for different routing thresholds.

Quick templates (working):
- Tier 0 template (one-line):
  "You are a concise assistant. Answer in <= 40 tokens. If unclear, ask 1 clarifying question."
- Tier 1 template (few-shot, 3 examples):
  "You are an assistant that answers customer support questions about billing. Examples:
   Q: I was charged twice for June. What happened?
   A: Apologize, confirm last 4 digits of card, check recent charge id 12345, offer refund timeline 3-5 business days.
   ... (2 more examples)
  Now answer: {user_question}"
- Tier 2 template (scaffold):
  "Decompose the problem into steps: 1) clarify facts, 2) list likely causes, 3) propose verification steps, 4) recommend next actions. Show reasoning briefly, then final answer."

Failure cases to watch for: 
- Exemplar leakage: examples too close and reveal PII. Need sanitization step.
- Cascading cost: naive thresholds send ~30% to Tier 2; adjust by precision of verifier.
- Semantic drift: Tier 0 answer style inconsistent with Tier 2; need style normalizer prompt or post-processing.

Metrics to capture in console + experiments:
- per-request token consumption (avg and tail), latency, QPS by tier
- verifier precision/recall, false positives that force promotion
- human-rated quality (5k sample) across tiers and aggregate system quality
- cost per solved/acceptable response (dollars)
- frequency of human escalation

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Var A: threshold on logprob (p>0.2 -> keep Tier0) vs Var B: reranker score threshold
- Var C: exemplar pool size 50 vs 500
- Var D: top-k exemplar 1 vs 3 vs 5
- Var E: allow Tier2 only for enterprise customers

Implementation notes / TODOs: 
- [ ] Mock harness + synthetic dataset (use last quarter support transcripts)
- [ ] Build small FAISS index and measure selection latency (target <15ms)
- [ ] Implement verifier baseline using server-side small model (gpt-2/mini) for speed test
- [ ] Add telemetry events: tier_selected, promote_reason, verifier_score, final_human_label
- [ ] Design rollout: start with Canary on non-critical routes for 2 weeks, compare cost/quality.

Edge considerations: 
- If exemplar selection fails (no close matches), degrade to Tier2 or generic safe response? Probably Tier2 for high-stakes, Tier0 fallback for low-stakes.
- Cache exemplar answers for repeated similar queries to cut cost. TTL tunable.
- GDPR: ensure exemplar store has no PII; need audit step.

Random experiment idea: "entropy gating" — compute response entropy on short probe completion; if high entropy, promote to next tier. Quick test to run.

Snippets to add to library (for later):
- small set of adaptive prompts for style bridging between tiers
- automatic brevity hints to control token tail
- prompt-level id + fingerprint to attribute quality regressions

Notes on UX: need transparent metrics in Console: percent by tier, cost delta, quality delta. Product should expose control knobs: max-tier-per-route, token-budget, verifier sensitivity.

Quick links: see linked_artifacts for related PRs/Confluence pages. Slack: #prompt-routing for ongoing convos.

Last: write up a short PRD blurb once we have 1k labelled examples. Keep this doc as living notebook.

-- Ava
